title: Edmund and the Compass
premise: In 1847, on the pearling coast of a colonial port, Tamsin Thornbury has spent her life measuring the world in what can be carried when the trading company that holds her indenture gives the orders. When a stranger named Edmund arrives carrying letters in the unmistakable handwriting of Captain Aldous Vane — officially drowned two years ago — he is pulled into a conspiracy of false deaths and stolen fortunes. Together they must smuggle Vane's evidence past three company checkpoints before the quarterly fleet sails and the proof is lost forever. Betrayal at the second checkpoint forces them to trust the very people the law calls criminals, and the story ends not with legal justice but with a quieter reckoning: the company's ledger burned, Tamsin's indenture voided by her own hand, and both of them choosing exile over belonging to anything that requires their silence.
about_author: Felix Marchetti is the pen name of a former merchant-marine clerk who spent six years cataloguing shipping manifests along colonial trade routes before turning to fiction. He writes historical novels about people the ledgers forgot.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Things
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She dives for pearl shell under her company indenture, cataloguing what she owns: a knife, a compass without its needle, her mother's silence. Establishes her habit of measuring everything by what can be carried. Emotional beat: quiet resignation sharpened by pride in her competence.

chapters.title: Orders Come at Dawn
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The company posts new orders: all incoming passengers searched at the customs house for contraband correspondence. Her foreman hints there's a reward for vigilance. She feels the net tightening around the harbor. Beat: unease disguised as duty.

chapters.title: A Stranger Off the Tide
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He steps off a coastal packet boat with salt-damaged boots and one possession that matters: letters in Captain Aldous Vane's handwriting — a man officially dead two years. He scans the checkpoints and understands he's already being watched. Beat: wary determination.

chapters.title: Handwriting of a Drowned Man
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, flashback-heavy. He explains how Vane, his old shipmate, smuggled the letters out over months, documenting the company faking deaths to void debts and claim estates. Vane has now gone silent. Beat: grief braided with obligation.

chapters.title: The Compass Without a Needle
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Searching passengers at the customs house, she notices Edmund's calm is rehearsed. Instead of reporting him, she lets him pass — then follows. Their first conversation is a duel of omissions. Beat: dangerous curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Company Owes
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The trading house's factor, Mr. Calloway, learns a passenger arrived asking about Vane. He doubles the checkpoint guards and offers Tamsin promotion for loyalty. Beat: menace dressed as opportunity.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He maps his route: the customs house, the toll bridge over the estuary, and the fleet gate where the quarterly ships load. Each has a different master, each can be bribed or survived. Beat: cold planning masking fear.

chapters.title: An Indenture Is a Chain
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She reads her own contract and finds the clause binding her until debt is cleared — a debt the company inflates yearly. Edmund's cause stops being abstract; it could be hers. Beat: anger discovering its own name.

chapters.title: The Needle Returns
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He recognizes Tamsin's broken compass as Vane's gift to her mother years ago — proof the families were entangled long before. He offers the missing needle he carries. Trust begins, conditionally. Beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: First Checkpoint: The Customs House
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Tamsin walks Edmund through as her 'hired porter,' using her inspector's authority against itself. A guard notes the extra crate. They clear it — barely. Beat: exhilaration curdling into exposure.

chapters.title: Calloway Summons the Fleet
chapters.summary: Calloway's POV (brief). He moves the fleet's departure up eight days, weaponizing the schedule. Anyone with evidence must run the remaining checkpoints in half the time. Beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: Night Market Bargains
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She trades her season's pearls to a smuggler named Brack for passage papers and a hiding place in a shell barge. The price is everything she owns. Beat: sacrifice made without ceremony.

chapters.title: The Letters Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. In Brack's loft, Tamsin finally hears the letters' contents: names, dates, forged death certificates — including a name she knows. Her father's drowning was no accident. Beat: personal grief detonating inside public injustice.

chapters.title: Whose Side Is the Law On
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They debate going to the magistrate; Edmund shows why every official is on the company's payroll. Justice will have to happen outside the law or not at all. Tamsin resists, then accepts. Beat: ideological turning point.

chapters.title: A Traitor in the Loft
chapters.summary: Brack's boy, paid by Calloway, copies a page of the evidence. Neither protagonist notices. Dramatic irony established. Beat: dread the reader feels before the characters do.

chapters.title: Second Checkpoint: The Toll Bridge
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The bridge is sealed; guards hold a copied page and are hunting 'a diver's child.' Tamsin's face is known. They split the evidence between them and cross separately — she through the water, he through the toll line. Beat: terror and trust intertwined.

chapters.title: Under the Estuary
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She free-dives beneath the bridge pilings with the letters oil-wrapped against her skin, nearly blacking out, saved by the discipline of a lifetime underwater. Beat: the body's competence redeeming the heart's fear.

chapters.title: The Interrogation of Edmund Roe
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Detained at the bridge, he talks his way through with a forged clerk's pass — but gives his real name to the sergeant, a mistake that will travel. Beat: victory shadowed by error.

chapters.title: Reunion in the Shell Barge
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Both survive; both confess their mistakes. The intimacy of shared failure deepens the bond. They learn the fleet now sails in four days. Beat: tenderness under pressure.

chapters.title: Calloway Offers a Price
chapters.summary: Calloway confronts Tamsin privately: her indenture voided, her mother's debts cleared, if she delivers Edmund and the letters. He genuinely believes he's offering mercy. Beat: temptation rendered almost reasonable.

chapters.title: The Mother Who Stayed Silent
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She confronts her mother, who knew about Vane and the falsified drownings and said nothing to keep Tamsin safe. Forgiveness is partial and hard. Beat: generational wound opened.

chapters.title: Brack's Choice
chapters.summary: Brack's POV. The smuggler, whose brother's name is in Vane's letters, decides the cause is his too. He burns his own safe-conduct papers to prove commitment. Beat: an outsider choosing belonging over survival.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: The Fleet Gate
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. First attempt: the gate is a fortress of company men, and Calloway himself inspects outgoing cargo. They withdraw without being seen — but the copied page means Calloway now knows exactly what the letters contain. Beat: strategic retreat, rising stakes.

chapters.title: Plan of the Desperate
chapters.summary: Group scene, Tamsin's POV mostly. New plan: hide the evidence in a pearl-shell shipment Tamsin herself is contracted to dive and pack — the one cargo never searched, because it's the company's own profit. Beat: audacity born of intimacy with the system.

chapters.title: Diving the Deep Bed
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She dives the dangerous outer bed to fill the shipment quota that will carry the letters, pushing her body past safety while Edmund tends the lines above. Beat: physical ordeal as emotional vow.

chapters.title: The Bentham Letter
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A final letter from Vane surfaces via Brack: Vane is alive, held on a company hulk offshore, and will be executed quietly once the fleet sails. Rescue and delivery now compete for the same hours. Beat: moral crisis — the man or the message.

chapters.title: We Do Not Leave Him
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She refuses to choose; the plan expands impossibly. Edmund, who came only to deliver paper, agrees to risk everything for a person. Beat: idealism hardened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Hulk at Anchor
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Night reconnaissance of the prison hulk: tides, sentries, the grate Vane described in his last letter. Brack provides a boat. Beat: suspense built from logistics.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Gate
chapters.summary: Calloway's POV. Using the copied page, he identifies the shell shipment and sets a trap at the fleet gate — but misjudges which barge. His trap catches Brack instead. Beat: antagonist's competence and first crack.

chapters.title: Brack Does Not Talk
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Brack endures questioning and buys them a day by feeding Calloway a false departure time. He pays with a beating and his boat. Beat: loyalty's cost made visible.

chapters.title: Rescue on the Turning Tide
chapters.summary: Edmund and Tamsin alternate. They board the hulk at slack tide, find Vane half-starved but lucid, and cut him out as the watch turns. A sentry dies; Edmund carries the weight of it. Beat: action climax part one, morally stained.

chapters.title: Vane Testifies to the Water
chapters.summary: Vane's POV briefly. Recovering in the loft, he insists the letters alone are insufficient — a living witness changes everything, but only if heard before the fleet sails and the colony's attention scatters. Beat: urgency renewed.

chapters.title: The Third Checkpoint, Second Attempt
chapters.summary: Full ensemble. With Vane hidden among shell crates and the letters sewn into Tamsin's diving suit, they walk into Calloway's trap knowingly. The false departure time splits the guards. Beat: climax part two — the gauntlet.

chapters.title: Calloway Unmasked
chapters.summary: Climax. At the gate, before assembled officers and the fleet's captain-superintendent, Tamsin produces the letters and Vane steps out alive. Calloway's forged certificates collapse under his own factor's testimony, bought by fear. Beat: justice outside the law, delivered publicly.

chapters.title: What the Law Cannot Give
chapters.summary: Falling action, dual POV. The superintendent buries the scandal to protect the trade; Calloway is quietly dismissed, not tried. No court, no restitution. The protagonists reckon with justice as exposure, not punishment. Beat: bitter clarity.

chapters.title: Burning the Ledger
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She takes her indenture ledger from the factor's office during the chaos of dismissal and burns it on the beach — not theft, she says, just arithmetic corrected. Her debt ceases to exist because its record does. Beat: liberation as an act, not a grant.

chapters.title: Vane Sails East
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Vane, restored enough to stand, chooses to leave on the fleet, taking copies of the letters to spread beyond one port's control. He and Edmund part as brothers who no longer need each other daily. Beat: release.

chapters.title: The Mother's Blessing
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Her mother, freed alongside her, chooses to stay in the port among the diving community. Tamsin realizes belonging was never the company — it was the people who stayed. Beat: reconciliation without erasure.

chapters.title: Two Tickets on a Coastal Packet
chapters.summary: Resolution. Edmund and Tamsin board the same small packet boat that brought him, carrying almost nothing — by design. She keeps the mended compass; he keeps the empty envelope. Beat: hope measured in what little they need.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Closing chapter, alternating final pages. At sea, Tamsin measures their possessions aloud and finds the list short and sufficient; Edmund begins writing a true account, unafraid of whose handwriting it bears. The coast recedes. Beat: peace earned, identity chosen, story closed.
